name: TLV76701DRVR
title: TLV767 1-A, 16-V precision linear voltage regulator
summary: The TLV767 is a positive linear regulator for loads up to 1 A, running from 2.5 V to 16 V at its input. The adjustable part (TLV76701) sets its output from 0.8 V to 14.6 V with two resistors against a 0.8 V reference; fixed parts cover 0.8 V to 6.6 V in 50 mV steps. Quiescent current is 50 µA typical and about 1.5 µA when disabled; the output holds 1 % over load and temperature. A 500 µs internal soft start, foldback current limiting, UVLO, thermal shutdown and an output discharge path are built in, and it is stable with 1 µF ceramic capacitors. Packages: 6-pin 2 mm × 2 mm WSON (DRV), 8-pin 3 mm × 3 mm HVSSOP (DGN) and 5-pin SOT-23 (DBV).
key_figures: 0.8 V to 14.6 V adjustable; 0.8 V to 6.6 V fixed, 50 mV steps

circuits.title: Typical application, adjustable output
circuits.description: The adjustable TLV767 set for 3.3 V out from a 5 V input at 100 mA. R1 from OUT to FB and R2 from FB to ground set the output against the 0.8 V feedback voltage: R1 / R2 = 3.125, and their sum stays under 660 kΩ so the FB current error is negligible. EN is tied to IN so the regulator runs whenever input is present. CIN and COUT are the ceramic input and output capacitors; CFF across R1 is optional.

parts.note: output capacitor, ceramic; 1 µF to 220 µF, 2 mΩ to 500 mΩ ESR

notes: The load-transient and PSRR curves for this design use COUT = 1 µF, with CFF = 10 pF and 0 pF respectively.
For load steps faster than 0.5 A/µs, COUT of 2.2 µF or more.

circuits.title: Reverse-current protection with a Schottky diode
circuits.description: A Schottky diode from OUT (anode) to IN (cathode) sits in parallel with the regulator's internal body diode. When the output is held above the input, the reverse current flows through the external diode rather than through the pass transistor's body diode. CIN and COUT are the usual input and output capacitors.

operation.text: The adjustable TLV76701 has an FB pin and takes an external divider for 0.8 V to 14.6 V out. Fixed versions have a SNS pin in place of FB and come from 0.8 V to 6.6 V in 50 mV steps. The SOT-23 (DBV) package exists in fixed versions only.

operation.topic: Internal divider of the fixed versions
operation.text: In a fixed part SNS feeds an internal divider: R1 is 531 kΩ or 1.062 MΩ, R2 between 66.9 kΩ and 8.5 MΩ, with 2 pF across R1. The error amplifier compares the divider tap with a 0.8 V reference.

EN is active high. Above the high threshold the output turns on; below the low threshold it turns off. An internal pull-up current (400 nA typical) keeps an open EN on, and EN can be wired to IN when no separate control is wanted. When disabled, an internal pulldown discharges the output.
Start-up uses an internal soft start of 500 µs typical. Together with the foldback current limit it keeps inrush current low during start-up, so less input capacitance is needed.

Dropout voltage is VIN – VOUT at the rated current with the pass transistor fully on, working as a switch in its ohmic region. Below the rated current dropout falls in proportion to the load. With the input below VOUT(nom) + VDO the output follows the input down.

The current limit is brickwall above VFOLDBACK (half the nominal output) and folds back below it. In brickwall mode the output current is held at ICL; as the output is pulled further towards ground the limit falls, reaching ISC with the output shorted. The output is not regulated while the limit acts. The pass transistor then dissipates (VIN – VOUT) × ICL in brickwall, or (VIN – VOUT) × ISC when shorted. If the heating trips thermal shutdown the part turns off, cools, and turns back on, cycling as long as the fault lasts.
A separate UVLO circuit watches VIN so the output turns on and off cleanly. Its hysteresis (130 mV typical) stops a dip in the input during turn-on from switching the regulator off again.

An output pulldown of 1.2 mA typical turns on when the part is disabled, and while 1.0 V < VIN < VUVLO. It is not meant to discharge a large output capacitance after the input has collapsed: current can then flow backward from output to input and damage the part.

The pass transistor turns off when the junction reaches TSD(shutdown), 180 °C typical, and back on when it cools to TSD(reset), 160 °C typical. Because the die's thermal time constant is short, the part can cycle on and off until dissipation drops. A large VIN – VOUT or the inrush charging a big output capacitor can trip it before start-up completes. Above the recommended maximum TJ the part no longer meets its specifications, and repeated shutdown or operation above that maximum reduces long-term reliability. The protection circuit is not a replacement for heat sinking.

The output regulates when VIN exceeds VOUT(nom) + VDO, the load is below the current limit, the junction is below the shutdown temperature, and EN has risen past its rising threshold and not since fallen below its falling threshold.

With the input below VOUT(nom) + VDO and everything else normal, the output tracks the input. Transient response is much worse in this state, since the pass transistor works as a switch, and line or load steps can move the output a long way. On leaving a steady dropout state (not during start-up) the output can overshoot briefly while the loop brings the pass transistor back into its linear region.
Pulling EN below the logic-low maximum shuts the output off: the pass transistor and internal circuits turn off and the output is discharged to ground internally.

The regulator is stable with low-ESR ceramic capacitors on input and output. X7R, X5R and C0G dielectrics hold their value well over temperature; Y5V is discouraged for its large capacitance swing. Effective capacitance can drop by up to half with bias and temperature, and the recommended values already allow for about 50 % of nominal.

No input capacitor is needed for stability, but one from IN to GND helps with reactive sources, transients, input ripple and PSRR; it is recommended when the source impedance is above 0.5 Ω. Fast large transients or a supply several inches away may need more. The output capacitor must lie within the recommended range for stability, and more of it improves dynamic response and reduces overshoot and undershoot.

Reverse current runs through the pass transistor's body diode, is not limited inside the part, and at high levels degrades reliability. It can arise when a large COUT is left with little load as the input collapses, when the output is driven before the input is up, or when the output is driven above the input; each can break the VOUT ≤ VIN + 0.3 V rating. Where it is expected, external protection is recommended, such as a Schottky diode from OUT to IN.

On the adjustable part a CFF from OUT to FB improves transient response, noise and PSRR but is not needed for stability unless the divider current is under 5 µA, when at least 10 pF is required. A larger CFF lengthens start-up; keeping CFF × R1 under 50 µs avoids that. With FB tied straight to OUT for 0.8 V, no CFF is fitted.

Dissipation is set by the input-to-output difference and the load, so the lowest input voltage that keeps regulation gives the least heat. Keep other heat sources away from the regulator. In packages with a thermal pad most heat leaves through the pad: solder it to a copper area with an array of plated vias to inner planes. RθJA from the thermal table is for the JEDEC standard board and depends strongly on copper area, weight and plane placement; ψJT and ψJB estimate TJ in a real board from a measured top or board temperature and depend little on copper area.
For 3.3 V out: with IFB = 50 nA the divider total must stay under 660 kΩ; R1 / R2 = 3.125 gives R2 ≤ 160 kΩ, so R2 = 160 kΩ, and R1 works out to 500 kΩ, taken as the standard 499 kΩ.

The input supply can be 2.5 V to 16 V. For good regulation and dynamic performance it should be at least VOUT(nom) + 1.5 V, and at least 3 V for 1 A operation. Use a low-impedance supply wired straight to IN.

Input and output capacitors sit right at the part. IN, OUT and GND run on copper planes for heat, with thermal vias stitched round the part. CIN lies beside IN and GND, COUT beside OUT, and on the adjustable part the divider and CFF beside FB, all over a ground plane.
